appliesToWhy: GA 3.1.1: the two rope exercises filed under push with handle rope and loadAxis across. face_pull and cable_crunch also use a rope (census need ropeLikely) but are in the pull and on-body archetypes and are not covered by this card.

loadAxis.basis: drawing decision from GA 3.1.1 (a rope can only be pulled, so the lever check is off); not a sourced claim, see gaps

handContact.text: Hand up against the knob at the end of the rope, one hand on each end.

grip.text: Neutral grip (palms facing each other), a full grip with the thumbs wrapped round the rope.

wrist.text: Straight, in line with the forearm, for the whole movement.

faults.label: Wrists curl
faults.what: The wrists bend toward the palms as the rope is pushed down.

gripLine.text: Hold each end of the rope, hands up against the knobs, palms facing each other, wrists straight.

claims.text: For the rope pushdown, hold the rope with each hand up against its clubbed end (the knob).

quotes.text: Grip the rope with your hand against the clubbed end.

claims.text: Grasp the handle or rope firmly with a full grip, thumbs clasped around it.

quotes.text: Attach the handle or rope and grasp it firmly with a full grip (thumbs clasped around the handle or rope).

claims.text: For the overhead extension the rope is held with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) behind the head. Using the same neutral grip for the rope pushdown is an inference: no source read states the palm direction for the pushdown.

quotes.text: Attach a rope to the low pulley. Stand facing away from the machine, holding the rope with a neutral grip, and step forward to create tension, positioning hands behind your head with elbows bent.

claims.text: In the rope pushdown the wrists stay straight for the whole movement, in line with the forearms.

quotes.text: Your wrists should be straight throughout the movement, press the handle down toward the floor to the extended position.
wrists in neutral positon (i.e., aligned with your forearms). This arm and wrist position should be maintained

claims.text: The overhead rope extension lists neutral wrist mobility as a requirement.

Bending the wrists (flexing them) as you push the weight down moves work from the triceps to the forearms, puts the wrists at a mechanical disadvantage and stresses the elbow; keep the wrists neutral. The source says this happens especially with the bar attachment; applying it to the rope is an inference.

quotes.text: Letting the forearms takeover is a little harder to catch but is just as common - especially when the bar attachment is used.
And this happens when you flex your wrists as you push the weight down.
This not only shifts tension away from the triceps and onto the forearms, but also:
puts your wrists at a mechanical disadvantage

sources.title: How to do Tricep Pushdowns with the Rope (NFPT)
Cable Rope Overhead Tricep Extension Low - Exercise Guide (Motra)
How To Get Bigger Triceps: 3 Training Mistakes You’re Probably Making (Built With Science)

gaps: GA 3.1.1 says the rope load sits in the fingers and on the little-finger edge of the fist, never on the heel of the palm. No source read says where the load sits in the hand; loadAxis "across" is kept as GA's drawing decision, not a claim.
Fault rope-slip (rope sliding out of the fist): no source read names it or says the knob stops it. Not drawn until sourced.

No source read gives a hand-contact or wrist rule specific to the overhead rope extension beyond the neutral grip (c3) and neutral wrist mobility (c5); the pushdown rules (c1, c2, c4) are applied to it by inference and need a source before an overhead sheet uses them.
notes: Same rules sourced in cards/rope_triceps_pushdown.json c2, c3, c5 (NFPT, ACE) and cards/overhead_cable_triceps_extension.json c3 (Motra). Re-read NFPT, ACE pushdown and Motra in full on 2026-10-01; quotes copied from that read. Built With Science (bws-tri) is new here.
ACE's pushdown steps cover both the handle and the rope ("handle / rope"), so c2 and c4 apply to the rope directly.
